title: NUJP: Lawyer’s ‘unintended’ intimidation can’t curtail rights

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—The National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP) said a lawyer’s apology for “unintended” intimidation cannot curtail the media’s right to report on suspicious transactions or corruption involving public officials. In a statement on Wednesday, the NUJP rejected the warning of lawyer Mark Vinluan, Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense lawyer, who claimed journalists could face criminal liability under the Anti-Money Laundering Act. Earlier, Vinluan cited penalties under the AMLA while questioning Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Secretariat Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura on rules governing financial confidentiality.
